findings.title: Delete and Pause menu items can never render in the ruler-free list view
findings.body: The menu now computes Delete/Pause abilities from the Prometheus rule (`grafanaDeleteAbility`, `grafanaPauseAbility`), but the rendering of those items is still gated on the ruler rule being present: `{canDelete && rulerRule && ...}` (line 165) and `{canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...}` (line 123). Since the new rule list (GrafanaRuleListItem -> RuleActionsButtons with only `promRule`) no longer loads ruler rules, `rulerRule` is always `undefined` there, so Delete and Pause disappear from the alert rule list menu even for users with permission. This is a user-visible regression: rules can no longer be deleted or paused from the list view. Either the gates must be relaxed to work from `promRule` (deriving the identifier/pause mutation from the Prometheus rule) or the actions must be hidden consistently with the computed abilities.

findings.title: "Silence notifications" menu item is a no-op when only a Prometheus rule is available
findings.body: `canSilence` in AlertRuleMenu is now satisfied by the Prometheus-rule abilities (`useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), so the "Silence notifications" item is rendered in the new list view. However the drawer is still rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true (line 104), and `rule` (the ruler rule) is `undefined` for list-view items that only pass `promRule`. Clicking the menu item therefore sets `showSilenceDrawer` but nothing ever opens — a dead menu entry. The GrafanaGroupLoader test asserts the item exists but never clicks it, so this is not caught. The drawer needs a path that works from the Prometheus rule (e.g. lazily fetch the ruler rule when opening) or the item must be hidden when no ruler rule is available.

findings.title: Missing React `key` on GrafanaRuleListItem in the filtered list
findings.body: In the `case 'grafana'` branch the newly used `<GrafanaRuleListItem>` is rendered without the `key={key}` prop that the previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader>` had (the other branches still pass `key`). The surrounding `rules.map(...)` produces a list, so React will log the "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warning and fall back to index-based reconciliation. Because this list is appended to incrementally during infinite scrolling, index-based reconciliation can reuse the wrong component instances (stale internal state such as open menus/drawers) for the wrong rule.

findings.title: Federated rule group check dropped from useAllAlertRuleAbilities
findings.body: `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` and treated federated groups as immutable, hiding Update/Delete/Pause. It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false` with a TODO. As a result every consumer of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (rules table, rule details, rule viewer) will now offer Edit/Delete for Mimir/Cortex federated rule groups (groups with `source_tenants`). Editing such a group through the UI, which has no notion of `source_tenants`, can silently drop the federation configuration on save. The federated check should be preserved (the group/`source_tenants` information is available on the CombinedRule) before merging.

findings.title: Grafana-managed recording rules lose Pause and Export abilities in the Prometheus ability hook
findings.body: `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` as the "is Grafana managed" flag for `Pause`, `ModifyExport`, `Restore` and `DeletePermanently`. The ruler-based equivalent used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for both Grafana alerting *and* Grafana recording rules. Grafana-managed recording rules support pausing and export, so after this change the list view will report Pause/ModifyExport as unsupported for them and the corresponding actions disappear. The flag should be `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for these abilities, with `alertingRule` reserved for alerting-only concerns such as Silence.

findings.title: Rule view link no longer carries the `returnTo` parameter
findings.body: The removed `GrafanaRuleLoader.GrafanaRuleListItem` built the href as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops the `returnTo` query parameter entirely. Consequently navigating from the rule list into a rule detail page loses the "return to previous" context, so the back/return affordance on the rule view will not bring the user back to the filtered list they came from. If this is intentional it should be stated; otherwise `createReturnTo()` should be re-added.

findings.title: Test codifies the missing Delete/Pause actions and never exercises Silence
findings.body: The new test asserts `menuItems.length).toBe(4)` (silence, copy link, duplicate, export) while the user has been granted `AlertingRuleDelete`/`AlertingRuleUpdate` both globally and on the folder. Delete and Pause are missing purely because AlertRuleMenu still requires a ruler rule to render them, so this assertion locks in the regression instead of detecting it. In addition, the `delete` selector added to `ui.menuItems` is never used, and the silence item is only asserted to exist — it is never clicked, which is why the non-functional silence drawer (it requires a ruler rule) goes unnoticed. The test should assert the full expected action set, including a click-through for Silence/Delete.

findings.title: Provisioned-rule protection in the new list depends on an untested optional `provenance` field
findings.body: `provenance` is added as an optional field on `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase` and is the only signal used by `isProvisionedPromRule` (utils/rules.ts) and `GrafanaRuleListItem`'s `isProvisioned` flag now that the ruler response is no longer fetched in the list view. If the Grafana Prometheus rules endpoint does not populate `provenance` (it is optional, so a missing value is silently falsy), provisioned/file-provisioned rules will be rendered as editable and expose Edit/Delete actions that the API will later reject. There is no test in this PR covering a provisioned Grafana rule in the list view; one should be added (and the API response confirmed to include `provenance`).

findings.title: logWarning is called from the render body on every render
findings.body: `getEditableIdentifier` is invoked directly during render and calls `logWarning('Unable to construct an editable rule identifier')` when neither a ruler rule nor a Grafana Prometheus rule is available (e.g. a data-source Prometheus rule with no ruler counterpart). Because this is a side effect inside render, the warning is emitted on every re-render (and twice per render under StrictMode) for each affected row, which can flood the analytics/log backend on a list page with many such rules. The logging should be moved into an effect or deduplicated.
